Key.Original: Run a local infrared illuminator at the operator, so a night-vision or infrared optic sees it and the unaided eye does not. A workshop idea re-implemented as AEE code; the mechanism has no published source. Local to the operator.

Key.English: Active IR Illuminator

Key.Original: Log thermal diagnostics to the RPT, including the wall-clock cost of each thermal function. Turn this on before reporting a performance fault.

Key.Original: Thermal Debug Log
Key.English: Thermal Debug Log

Key.Original: Seconds between object-temperature scans. Surface temperatures change on time constants of 600 seconds and longer, so a scan every tick is wasted work. 0 scans every tick.
Key.English: Seconds between object-temperature scans. Surface temperatures change on time constants of 600 seconds and longer, so a scan every tick is wasted work. 0 scans every tick.

Key.Original: Object Scan Interval
Key.English: Object Scan Interval

Key.Original: The host channel for the thermal display. Vanilla TI runs the display on the engine's own thermal channel overlaid on the vehicle's native TI. DTV disables the vehicle's native TI and draws the display over the day channel instead, the route the proven A3TI and MKK thermal mods use, so the engine's TI pass cannot fight the mod's. DTV is vehicle-only: the player must be in a vehicle optic. It is a prototype for comparison and is the only channel that does not set the ppEffectForceInNVG flag.

Key.English: Thermal Base Channel

Key.Original: Log thermal system diagnostics (second sun, building paint, AGC) to the RPT. Thermal's own debug flag - not nightvision's.

Key.Original: Thermal Diagnostics
Key.English: Thermal Diagnostics

Key.Original: Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. Local normalises each object to its own selection range: it widens that object's internal contrast, but it breaks comparison between objects because a hot and a cold object can map to the same ramp. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast.
Key.English: Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast.

Key.Original: Hot end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Set it high to keep fires and exhaust on scale. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure.

Key.Original: Cold end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Used in manual display mode and as the fallback before the scene AGC is ready. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure.

Key.Original: Ember interpolates the engine's own decoded thermal colours through a continuous ramp. White hot grey is the luminance form of the same ramp. The isotherm modes are the MKK thermal highlight colours as procedural two-tone ramps: a body below the display window midpoint stays cold, a body at or above it takes the mode hue (red, green, yellow, magenta or sepia).
